| Spec | Requirement | Scenario | Asserting test(s) |

| notification-channels | Channel contract | Blocked outcome | `telegram-channel.test.ts` → 403 maps to `blocked`; `telegram.test.ts` → 403 |
| notification-channels | Scheduler depends only on the interface | No provider coupling | `reminder-scan.test.ts` → `reminders.ts` never matches `/telegram/i` + import allowlist (`./notification-channel` only, type-only) |
| notification-channels | Seam proven with a fake channel | Scheduler tested against a fake | `reminders.test.ts` → entire `runReminderPoll` suite (fake channel + in-memory repo, zero network/credentials) |
| notification-channels | Additional channels are additive | New provider added later | Structural: `reminder-scan.test.ts` → contract file imports nothing and never names a provider; `telegram-channel.ts` is a standalone binding — a new channel adds a file without touching the scheduler |
| record-visibility | Notification isolation | Only creator notified | `reminders.test.ts` → creator-only send test (linked peer gets nothing) |
| record-visibility | Notification isolation | Admin read notifies no one | `reminder-scan.test.ts` → the single `.send(` call site in non-test `src/` is `lib/reminders.ts`; no `app/` or `components/` file sends |
| record-visibility | Notification isolation | Peer view notifies no one | same scan test (`.send(` allowlist) |
| record-visibility | Notification isolation | Search and calendar notify no one | same scan test (`.send(` allowlist) |
| reminder-delivery | Eligibility | Due record fires | `reminders.test.ts` → `isEligible` due-inside-window cases |
| reminder-delivery | Eligibility | Missing date or time never notifies | `reminders.test.ts` → empty date / empty time cases |
| reminder-delivery | Eligibility | Terminal status skipped | `reminders.test.ts` → `done` / `cancelled` cases |
| reminder-delivery | Eligibility | Outside late window skipped | `reminders.test.ts` → >24 h late window case |
| reminder-delivery | Poll cadence | Delivered near schedule | `appwrite/reminders.test.ts` → exact `listDue` wire query (status/between/orderAsc/limit) + `reminders.test.ts` window boundaries (inclusive endpoints, midnight/month/year) |
| reminder-delivery | Creator-only delivery | Only creator notified | `reminders.test.ts` → `runReminderPoll` sends exactly one pair `(creator chat, Recordatorio: …)` |
| reminder-delivery | Notified marking | Marked after success | `reminders.test.ts` → delivered ⇒ `markNotified` called + memory state flips; `appwrite/reminders.test.ts` → wire write `{ notified: true }` |
| reminder-delivery | Notified marking | Unnotified after failure | `reminders.test.ts` → transient outcome leaves `notified` untouched, no mark |
| reminder-delivery | Notified marking | No duplicate after restart | `reminders.test.ts` → fresh run over persisted `notified: true` sends 0 |
| reminder-delivery | Send failure and retry | Transient failure retried | `reminders.test.ts` → first poll transient (unmarked), second poll re-sends and marks |
| reminder-delivery | Restart safety | Resume after restart | `reminder-runner.test.ts` → `Symbol.for` guard (one loop pair per process), SIGTERM stop/abort, backoff reset on success; offset restart re-delivery covered by `pollBotOnce` transient-keeps-offset tests |
| reminder-delivery | Disabled or unconfigured reminders | App boots without env | `env.test.ts` → `loadReminderEnv()` never throws, missing keys ⇒ `{ enabled: false, reason }`; `reminder-runner.test.ts` → disabled env starts 0 timers and logs one line |
| reminder-delivery | Disabled or unconfigured reminders | Disabled by environment | `env.test.ts` → `REMINDERS_ENABLED=false` ⇒ disabled; runner test → 0 timers. (Env-level coverage; poll-level counterpart: `reminders.test.ts` "zero sends while no subscription is active") |
| task-listing | Telegram linking entry point | Open linking page | `telegram-view.test.ts` → `telegramEntry(...).href === '/telegram'` for every state; rendered by `app/page.tsx` |
| task-listing | Telegram linking entry point | Entry present when unlinked | `telegram-view.test.ts` → label+href present for **all four** states |
| task-listing | Telegram linking entry point | Entry shows current status | `telegram-view.test.ts` → linked ⇒ badge `Vinculado`; failed status read ⇒ `Sin vincular`, never throws |
| telegram-linking | Link initiation | Mint link | `telegram-link.test.ts` → 32-byte/43-char token, 10-min TTL, repo write, re-mint kills previous link |
| telegram-linking | Link initiation | Expired token rejected | `telegram-link.test.ts` → past-TTL rejected without write (+1 ms inside window accepted) |
| telegram-linking | Bot callback validation | Successful exchange | `telegram-link.test.ts` → one write stores chat id + activates + consumes; `route.test.ts` → 200 |
| telegram-linking | Bot callback validation | Reused token rejected | `telegram-link.test.ts` → consumed token rejected, link unchanged; `route.test.ts` → 404 uniform body |
| telegram-linking | Bot callback validation | Missing secret header rejected | `route.test.ts` → 401 without touching storage (wrong length + wrong value) |
| telegram-linking | Link status and unlink | Status shown | `telegram-view.test.ts` → linked copy title `Vinculado`; page (`app/telegram/page.tsx`) renders it |
| telegram-linking | Link status and unlink | Unlink | `telegram-link.test.ts` → `unlinkTelegramLink` resets `chatId/active/token/tokenExpiresAt` and keeps `userId`; `appwrite/telegram.test.ts` → wire shape of `unlink` |

**Coverage: 34/34 scenarios have ≥1 asserting test; 17/17 requirements covered.**

## 8.3 Isolation guard

| Check | Evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|
| No `crm-ge` / `ecotech_sitio_web` changes | `git status --porcelain -- crm-ge ecotech_sitio_web` → empty; all commits touch `src/`, `README.md`, `openspec/changes/agenda-reminders/` | ✅ |
| `.send(` call sites | non-test `src/` grep → exactly `src/lib/reminders.ts:183` (the scheduler). Note: task 8.3's wording named `reminder-runner.ts`/`telegram-channel.ts`; the implemented rule is stronger — the ONLY `.send(` in the whole app is the scheduler, enforced by `reminder-scan.test.ts` | ✅ |
| `TELEGRAM_*` never `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` | grep across `src/` + `.env.example` → zero matches | ✅ |
| `TELEGRAM_*` never logged | non-test console sites: `reminder-runner.ts` (generic `defaultLog` → `describeError` = method+status only), `instrumentation.ts` (start failure message). Unit tests assert `TelegramCallError` and the link flow never stringify token/chat id/URL | ✅ |
| Live `agenda.tasks` safety | Phase 1 read-only check: exactly the 2 pre-existing records (`prueba 1`, `pagar el agua`) survive; no enumeration-delete anywhere (create/update/patch only) | ✅ |

## 8.4 / 8.5 — BLOCKED UNTIL HUMAN (unchecked on purpose)

- **8.4**: create the bot via @BotFather, generate `TELEGRAM_LINK_SECRET`
  (`openssl rand -hex 32`), set `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME`,
  `TELEGRAM_LINK_SECRET` in `.env.local` and on the Easypanel service.
  All code paths are token-free with fakes; nothing faked here.
- **8.5**: live end-to-end (deploy → mint → `/start` → confirmation → one
  message → `notified=true` → restart no-duplicate → unlink). Depends on 8.4.

## 8.6 Rollback drill (documented, not executed)

`REMINDERS_ENABLED=false` → both loops stop (unit-tested: disabled env ⇒ 0
timers) and the app is otherwise unaffected; full revert = reverse-order PR
revert. Documented in `README.md` → "Telegram reminders → Rollback" (task 7.8).
